### 2026-09-23 — greenhouse-watch · fix: justification lines now sum to the score
Found while building the INFO 7375 Professor Bear demo on Figma (persona Aarav): a London ML
role showed lines +3.0, +3.0, +1.0, −1.0 (= 6.0) against score 3.5. Scoring was correct; the
report was not. (1) The title weight is credited once, but a line printed "+3.0" for every
matching résumé title; repeats now read "(already counted, +0)". (2) The `skill_any` bonus
(+0.5) was added but never printed; it now has its own line. New test
`test_justification_lines_sum_to_score` fails on the old script (lines 10.0 vs score 7.5)
and passes on the new; 23 tests pass. Verdicts and scores are unchanged, so earlier runs'
decisions stand; only their printed justifications under-explained them.

### 2026-10-21 — ms-is-swe-opt-shortlist · Mode Build sample run
Recipe `ms-is-swe-opt-shortlist` v0.2.0 (RUNNABLE-SAMPLE; 4 TODOs open, all proposed additions outside the run). Inputs: `course/2026fa/submissions/Vrajesh-works/mode-build/postings-2026-10-21.json` (12 entries), `--as-of 2026-10-21 --opt-start 2027-01-15` (placeholder dates), 80 Days CSV sha256 `eccdee2a…6270` (30,369 rows, newest funding 2025-09-26, 390 days before the as-of date). Outputs: `mode-build/runs/shortlist-log.json`, `shortlist-report.md`, scorer `role-scores.json/.md`. Result: `3/12 scored · Apply 1 · Consider 0 · Skip 2 (skip 67%)`; 2 excluded by a human (citizenship, clearance); 1 opt-bridge-open; 2 not-in-csv; 4 no-posting network targets. `npm run ats:liveness`: 6 active, 1 expired (Intuit, HTTP 404; company not in CSV so no decision changed). **Defect:** it printed Cohere Health active, but the student opened the page ("no longer open"); Greenhouse redirects removed jobs to the board with HTTP 200. Cohere typed `dead` by a person and the run redone (first run: Apply 1 · Consider 1 · Skip 1). Engine script not changed; defect not yet reported upstream. Break attempts: dead posting → Skip/network; `--as-of` after window → all Skip; impossible date and tracked out-dir → exit 2. 17 tests pass; `npm run verify` passes. **Gate G4:** Vrajesh Mathurbhai Nasit reopened the Verkada and Motion Recruitment postings on 2026-10-21 and confirmed both live (stated in session; the program's JSON `human_gate` field is unchanged). Open: unscored dead postings are not flagged; data is 390 days old; "entry-level" unverifiable; funding not a scorer input.

## Student entries (Assignment 5)

assignment, not a precedent for future run entries (which still belong in
`logs/runs/<term>-<handle>-<n>.md`, as this student's Assignment 3 work already

### 2026-10-29 — Assignment 5 Setup Exercise: search/ personal data layer

Built `search/resume.json`, `search/profile.yml`, and `search/gaps.md` — the
personal data layer for this fork. `search/private-notes.md` is gitignored per
Step 0.

**Three attestation errors caught and fixed in resume.json, all three by Pratham
directly, with no AI involved in finding any of them:** (1) Full-Stack Developer
(Sep-Dec 2022) was mis-sequenced ahead of Moonlighting (Jan-Jul 2023), breaking
reverse-chronological order; (2) the agent silently assumed University of
Mumbai's GPA was a native 3.5/4.0 without asking — Pratham caught this and
supplied the actual resolving fact: it's his own conversion from a 10-point
Indian CGPA, which no AI could have known; (3) two ongoing projects had
`end_date: "present"`, mixing a word into a date-typed field — now `end_date:
null` plus an explicit `status` field. (A review of an earlier draft of this
entry incorrectly credited Claude (claude.ai) with flagging (2) and (3); checked
against the actual conversation record, both were Pratham's own direct catches,
and that incorrect attribution is corrected here.) Named plainly, not glossed
over: (1) and (3) are formatting/schema fixes, not errors about Pratham's actual
history; only (2) is a real error about him. A further pass specifically hunted
for stronger candidates —
the project `type`/`team_size` fields ("open-source," "solo," agent-inferred, not
stated), the Moonlighting "Software Engineer" title (could have been a promoted
internship), and the identical 15% PostgreSQL figure on both University of Mumbai
entries (could have been a copy-paste duplicate) — and Pratham confirmed all three
accurate on direct review, so they're recorded here as checked, not left silent,
even though none became a fourth correction.

**Top gap (gaps.md):** no visible evidence of correctness testing, especially for
the concurrency bug fixed at Swapt — cited to Cursor's New Grad 2027 posting's
explicit correctness bar, not an assumption.

**Killed row:** "Hands-on model-training / ML-research experience" — the agent's
evidence cell said "industry assumption," which is exactly the invented-demand-
signal failure this table is supposed to catch; neither posting actually checked
(Palantir, Cursor) asks for model training.

**Removed row:** "No track record inside a large engineering org's review/design
process." Claude (claude.ai) flagged, across both of its review passes on
`gaps.md`, that this evidence described mentorship Palantir *offers*, not
experience it *requires* — catching the real problem first. Claude Code's own
re-check, prompted by that flag, then found the underlying cause: the evidence
cell conflated two different job postings (citing mentorship language from one
posting while sourcing its URL from another, actually-fetched one), and the
posting actually fetched (Palantir) doesn't require prior large-org experience at
all — Pratham's real record appears to meet what it actually asks for. Removed
rather than patched, since a gaps.md evidence cell that doesn't support its own
gap is the exact failure this table exists to prevent.

**profile.yml field corrected from the agent's first draft:** `target_role.primary`
contradicted `company_size_range` and `industry.target_sectors` (said "seed-Series
D" while the other two fields included big tech, fintech, and consumer tech) —
widened the sentence to match the real, broader search instead of narrowing the
other fields.

**Verification check (Step 4), answered honestly:**
- resume.json: Most entries trace to a real résumé PDF plus one confirmed
  second-source correction (the Sep-Dec 2022 role). Several skills in the
  `skills` block have no supporting bullet anywhere in the record — GCP, Java,
  Gemini, Groq, RAG, and pgvector are all listed but never demonstrated in a
  job or project bullet. Asked directly, Pratham chose to keep them listed
  as-is rather than add a bullet or remove them — a known, named gap between
  the skills list and the bullets, not a hidden one.
  InferMesh's "114 Go tests" and all of Orqen's bullets are self-report only,
  flagged as such in the file's own `agent_note` fields, not asserted as
  verified. Sutriva's test count was independently re-verified and is the
  strongest catch in this exercise, not the list-order fix originally
  highlighted here: three different numbers (87, 98, then 111) surfaced across
  different resume drafts and different points in this exercise before a
  direct, live `pnpm test` run under the required Node version settled which
  one was actually true.
- profile.yml: `stem_eligible` is marked `uncertain`, not `yes` — no DSO
  confirmation exists yet. OPT dates are explicitly marked `planned`/`estimate`,
  and the hard gate value (`opt_end_date`) uses the *estimated* 12-month
  baseline, not the hoped-for STEM-extended date — "estimated," not
  "confirmed," which an earlier version of this entry incorrectly said.
- gaps.md: Not every row cited something real, on this draft or an earlier one —
  one row ("hands-on model-training") invented a demand signal from assumption
  rather than a posting or O*NET entry, and a second row's citation (the
  large-org track-record gap) turned out to conflate two different postings and
  was removed outright once checked, rather than patched. Neither slipped
  through to the final file. The one open gap remaining (correctness testing)
  cites Cursor's posting directly, and the one closed gap (reviewable links)
  also traces to Cursor's posting — no row currently cites O*NET; an earlier
  version of this entry incorrectly said one did.

This entry itself went through two rounds of claude.ai review before this final
version — the first round caught the skills/depth gaps above; a second round
caught that this entry's own prose had drifted out of sync with the files it
describes (a stale O*NET citation claim, an overclaimed "confirmed" on an
estimated date) after those files were revised. Both are fixed above.
